newsitem.title: UK: Lord Donaldson criticises Sea Empress report delay.
newsitem.headline: Lord Donaldson criticises Sea Empress report delay.

text.p: Lord Donaldson, who headed the UK inquiry into the grounding of the oil tanker Braer, on Wednesday criticised delays in publication of the report into the Sea Empress.

Lord Donaldson said: "The failure of the Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) to publish its report even within a year of the incident has denied us lessons which undoubtedly will be available once the true facts are known."
"I regard this delay as a very serious matter. The United Kingdom government has an international obligation to investigate and report on such incidents and time is of the essence."
The Sea Empress spilled some 70,000 tonnes of oil when it grounded off Milford Haven port in south Wales in February 1996.
Lord Donaldson was speaking at a seminar organised by the International Salvage Union in London considering the stationing of tugs by government to deal with incidents such as the Braer grounding.
The MAIB sent its report into the Sea Empress for final responses from those affected by it in January 1997.
Lord Donaldson said: "This procedure is required by the regulations, but is wholly misguided.

"It gives the recipients unrivalled opportunities for re-arguing their respective cases on the facts, on the inferences to be drawn from those facts and on the issue of blameworthiness. It gives them the right to suggest a re-writing of large chunks of the report," he said.

Ministers had previously pledged that the report would be completed by February, according to Britain's opposition Labour party which has accused the government of deliberately trying to delay the report's publication until after the May 1 election.

A Department of Transport spokesperson told Reuters before the general election was called that publication of the Sea Empresss report could be around the end of March, but that it still had to be submitted to the Secretary of State.
Lord Donaldson added that he did not want to attribute blame to the delays in the report, and he said noone should be criticised without having a right to reply.
- Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + Tel 171 542 4087
